es: Escribir un párrafo que llegue a una conclusión prudente a partir de tres pistas, descarte una alternativa con una prueba y cierre con una valoración matizada (on balance).

teaching.en: There is a ladder outside the café and a strong smell of paint, but each observation is only a clue, not a conclusion.
teaching.es: Hay una escalera fuera de la cafetería y un fuerte olor a pintura, pero cada observación es solo una pista, no una conclusión.
teaching.explanationEs: Primera pieza: las pistas son datos observables, descritos sin interpretarlos.

teaching.en: Taken together, these clues make a renovation the most plausible explanation, although we should not speculate beyond what we can see.
teaching.es: En conjunto, estas pistas hacen de unas obras la explicación más plausible, aunque no debemos especular más allá de lo que vemos.
teaching.explanationEs: Segunda pieza: una conclusión prudente con plausible, suggest o probably.
segments: Taken together, these clues make a renovation the most plausible explanation,

teaching.en: Apparently, the owner has ordered a new sign, which suggests that the café intends to reopen rather than close for good.
teaching.es: Al parecer, el dueño ha encargado un letrero nuevo, lo que sugiere que la cafetería piensa reabrir en lugar de cerrar para siempre.
teaching.explanationEs: Apparently marca información oída o vista que aún no se ha comprobado.
segments: Apparently, the owner has ordered a new sign, which suggests that
the café intends to reopen rather than close for good.
teaching.audioText: Apparently, the owner has ordered a new sign, which suggests that the café intends to reopen rather than close for good.

teaching.en: We can rule out the alternative that the café is closing permanently, because a business in trouble rarely pays for a new sign.
teaching.es: Podemos descartar la alternativa de que la cafetería cierre definitivamente, porque un negocio en apuros rara vez paga un letrero nuevo.
teaching.explanationEs: Rule out + alternativa + because + prueba: descartar siempre lleva su razón.
segments: We can rule out the alternative that the café is closing permanently,
because a business in trouble rarely pays for a new sign.

teaching.en: On balance, the evidence favours a renovation, yet a cautious writer would add that a final answer needs a statement from the owner.
teaching.es: En conjunto, las pruebas favorecen unas obras, pero un autor cauteloso añadiría que una respuesta final necesita una declaración del dueño.
teaching.explanationEs: On balance: valoración final matizada tras sopesar las pistas; no es una certeza.

teaching.en: Each clue on its own is weak and often inconclusive, but several clues that point the same way make a far stronger case than a single striking one.
teaching.es: Cada pista por sí sola es débil y suele ser no concluyente, pero varias pistas que apuntan en la misma dirección forman un caso mucho más sólido que una sola llamativa.
teaching.explanationEs: Varias pistas coincidentes pesan más que una sola, por llamativa que sea.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que recoge una pista sin interpretarla.

choices.text: The shop has definitely closed for good.
There are boxes at the door and a van outside.
The owner is moving the goods to another town.

feedback.es: Una pista es un dato observable (cajas, furgoneta); las otras frases ya interpretan más de lo que se ve.

hint.es: Una pista describe lo que ves, no lo que supones.

origin.text: From the pavement you notice three things: the lights are off, there are boxes on the ground by the door, and a van is parked outside with its engine running.

prompt.es: Completa: «Las obras son la explicación más plausible.»

feedback.es: Plausible expresa que una explicación es verosímil sin afirmarla como hecho.

origin.text: A renovation is the most ___ explanation, because the ladder, the smell of paint and the covered windows all point the same way.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Podemos descartar la lluvia porque la calle está seca.»

answer.text: We can rule out rain because the street is dry

feedback.es: Rule out + alternativa + because + prueba: se descarta con un dato.

hint.es: Rule out lleva la alternativa detrás.

prompt.es: Elige la conclusión más prudente a partir de las tres pistas.

choices.text: These clues prove that the shop has closed for good.
These clues show that the owner is hiding something.
These clues suggest that the shop is being painted.

feedback.es: Con pocas pistas solo cabe una conclusión prudente con suggest; prove y show afirman más de lo que permiten los datos.

origin.text: There is a ladder against the wall, the air smells of paint, and the windows have been dark for three days, although a light is on inside.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cada pista por sí sola es débil» y «no podemos descartar esa posibilidad».

feedback.es: Clue es la pista individual y rule out la expresión para descartar una posibilidad con una prueba.

sentences: Each ___ on its own is weak, but several together make a strong case.
We cannot ___ out that possibility yet, because we have no proof.

prompt.es: Escucha las pistas y elige la conclusión del hablante.

choices.text: He thinks that a shop will probably open soon.
He is certain that the shop is closing down.
He believes that the van is delivering stolen goods.

feedback.es: Las luces, la furgoneta y el papel en las ventanas sugieren una apertura próxima, pero el hablante se cubre: no apostaría por ello.

origin.audio: The lights are on at midnight, there is a delivery van outside, and the windows are covered with paper. I think the new shop is getting ready to open, although I would not promise it, because the paper could also mean that somebody is building something.

prompt.es: Escribe un párrafo con tres pistas, una conclusión y una alternativa descartada.

answer.text: The bakery on our street has been closed for five days, and I have noticed three clues. First, there is a delivery van at the door. Second, the front wall has been freshly painted. Third, somebody saw the owner with a new sign yesterday. Taken together, these clues suggest that the bakery is having a renovation, which seems the most plausible explanation. We can rule out the alternative that it is closing for good, because nobody buys a new sign and paints a wall again before leaving. Apparently, the owner wants to reopen soon. On balance, I think we should not speculate any further; I will ask him tomorrow to be sure.
accepted: The bakery on our street has been closed for five days, and I have noticed three clues. First, there is a delivery van at the door. Second, the front wall has been freshly painted. Third, somebody saw the owner with a new sign yesterday. Taken together, these clues suggest that the bakery is having a renovation, which seems the most plausible explanation. We can rule out the alternative that it is closing for good, because nobody buys a new sign and paints a wall again before leaving. Apparently, the owner wants to reopen soon. On balance, I think we should not speculate any further; I will ask him tomorrow to be sure.

The bakery has been shut for five days, so I looked for clues. There is a van parked outside, the front has new paint and the owner was carrying a new sign yesterday. These clues point to a renovation, and I think that is the most likely explanation, although I may be wrong. The alternative that it is closing permanently is unlikely, so I can rule it out: nobody orders a new sign and repaints a wall before leaving. Apparently, the owner plans to reopen soon. On balance, it would be unwise to speculate; I will ask him tomorrow to be sure.

feedback.es: El párrafo debe describir las tres pistas, concluir con prudencia, descartar el cierre definitivo con la prueba del letrero y cerrar con una valoración matizada.

origin.text: La panadería de tu barrio lleva cinco días cerrada. Pistas: hay una furgoneta de reparto en la puerta, han pintado la fachada y ayer vieron al dueño con un letrero nuevo. Escribe en inglés un párrafo de 140 a 190 palabras: describe las tres pistas, da una conclusión prudente (suggest, probably, plausible…), descarta una alternativa (por ejemplo, que cierre para siempre) con una prueba y termina con una valoración matizada.

prompt.es: Completa: «Al parecer, el dueño vendió el local la semana pasada.»

feedback.es: Apparently introduce lo que parece cierto por lo que se ha oído, pero no está comprobado.

origin.text: ___, the owner sold the shop last week. Nobody has confirmed it, so for the moment it may be no more than a rumour.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que descarta la alternativa con una prueba adecuada.

choices.text: We can rule out a break-in, because break-ins are quite rare in this area.
We can rule out a break-in, because the door is not damaged and nothing is missing.
We can rule out a break-in, because the lights are off now.

feedback.es: Una alternativa se descarta con una prueba concreta del caso (puerta sin daños, nada falta), no con una estadística general ni con un dato irrelevante.

origin.text: The shop is dark and the lights are off. Some neighbours think that somebody broke in, but the front door is not damaged, nothing is missing from the window, and the alarm company received no signal.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué actitud muestra el hablante ante su propia conclusión.

choices.text: He is certain that the house is his own.
He thinks that the question is not worth asking.
He sees it as likely but wants more proof.

feedback.es: Dice seems likely y pide ver el recibo antes de afirmar más: su conclusión es probable, pero cautelosa.

origin.audio: I walked past the house on Elm Street this morning. There is paint on his shoes, a ladder in his car and a new colour on the wall. Did he paint his house? It seems likely, although it could just as easily be a friend's house, and I would want to see the receipt before I said any more. Of course, I may simply be wrong.

prompt.es: Elige la conclusión con el verbo más prudente.

choices.text: The lights and the car suggest that someone may be at home.
The lights and the car prove that someone is hiding inside.
The lights and the car mean that nobody lives there now.

feedback.es: Con luces y un coche solo cabe una posibilidad (suggest + may); prove y mean afirman lo que los datos no permiten.

origin.text: The lights are on and a car is parked outside, but nobody has answered the doorbell for two hours.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En conjunto, esa alternativa resulta muy poco probable.»

answer.text: On balance that alternative seems very unlikely

feedback.es: On balance abre una valoración final matizada; unlikely la expresa sin cerrarla del todo.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sería imprudente especular sobre los motivos antes de hablar con el dueño.»

feedback.es: Speculate es opinar sin pruebas suficientes: justo lo que un párrafo prudente evita.

origin.text: We have too little information to decide. It would be a mistake to ___ about the reasons before the owner has spoken to us.
